data.body:
=== FIX LANDED LOCALLY, GREEN, MUTATION-CHECKED. 727f AND d103 ARE ONE CHANGE. ===

WHAT CHANGED

`reconcile_helpers.drop_snapshot_echo_field_updates` is generalised and renamed to
`drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions`. It now drops BOTH arms whose correctness depends
on `local_state` genuinely being local state, matched on a `(direction, action, reason)` triple
AND a mandatory `provenance["source"] == "differ"` conjunct:

    ("outbound", "update", "field_drift")    <- 727f
    ("outbound", "create", "unbound_local")  <- d103

`differ.compute_mutations` is NOT touched; the suppression stays at the one call site so the
documented local-vs-jira contract survives intact for callers that honour it. Both
`differ.py`'s module docstring and `run_differs`'s docstring now record that the sole production
caller never migrated, and both carry an explicit note that the suppression must be REMOVED in
the same change if that caller is ever migrated (d103 acceptance criterion 3).

COMPLETENESS — the fix is exhaustive for this call site, not just for the two observables.
Fed a realistic fetched-snapshot pair (a key only in prev, a key changed between prev and curr,
an unchanged key, and a key only in curr), `compute_mutations` can emit exactly three things:

    (inbound,  create, jira_new)        <- CORRECT here; preserved
    (outbound, create, unbound_local)   <- suppressed
    (outbound, update, field_drift)     <- suppressed

The differ's other local_state-dependent arms (`duplicate_local_id`, `ambiguous_local_binding`,
`dangling_jira_local_id`, and the absent-partner probes) are UNREACHABLE from a fetched snapshot,
exactly as d103 predicted: they read `local_id` / `jira_key` fields a fetched snapshot entry never
carries. So there is no residual wrong emission left behind at this call site.

RED -> GREEN. Four oracles, each seen RED against origin/main with a failure message naming the
mechanism, then GREEN:
 * diffing/test_snapshot_differ_stale_local_state.py
     ::test_a_converged_pair_plans_no_outbound_update_after_our_own_write   (727f, diff phase)
     ::test_a_key_that_left_the_fetch_window_plans_no_outbound_create       (d103, diff phase)
 * orchestrate/test_reconcile_once.py
     ::test_real_field_change_converges_after_one_pass                      (727f, live path)
     ::test_a_key_absent_from_the_current_snapshot_never_reaches_create_issue (d103, live path,
       asserts at the TRANSPORT — client.create_issue is never called)
Positive controls, green throughout: the inbound create for a brand-new remote key still plans,
and an invariant SEED mutation survives (the seed deliberately reuses the `field_drift` reason
string, so a suppression keyed on reason alone would eat it).

MUTATION CHECKS — three, each verified to fail for the RIGHT reason:
 1. remove `("outbound","update","field_drift")` from the suppressed set -> exactly the two 727f
    oracles go RED with the phantom-echo message; both d103 oracles stay GREEN.
 2. remove `("outbound","create","unbound_local")` -> exactly the two d103 oracles go RED with
    the resurrect message; both 727f oracles stay GREEN.
 3. remove the `source == "differ"` conjunct -> exactly the seed-mutation control goes RED.
No mutation produced an AttributeError or an import failure, so none of these is the invalid kind
of mutation recorded on this ticket earlier.

GATES: `make lint` clean, `make typecheck` clean (407 files), `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler`
1808 passed. `run_differs.py` is 779 lines, under the 800 cap.

The fix was implemented by a subagent that never saw the oracles — the three test files were
moved out of its working tree and declared off-limits, and were byte-compared against a held-aside
copy after it finished. It was given the contract (the postconditions) and not the assertions.
